annotations.text:
Motion (all of it loops, so it is alive whenever you look):
· Painting drifts slowly (38s Ken Burns); the red and green curtain cutouts sway against it as separate parallax layers.
· Index fragments settle from scattered 3D depth into the card, then the whole constellation keeps breathing in perspective (16s orbit) while each chip floats on its own period; the card carries a slow sheen sweep.
· In production the settle is scroll-driven (pinned ~2 viewport heights, CSS scroll timeline); reduced motion renders the settled state with no loops.
· Depth is CSS perspective + rotate3d only — no WebGL. Ease cubic-bezier(0.22, 1, 0.36, 1).
· Art: Vermeer, public domain — the repo's existing Correspondence plates from landing/art.

Two hero directions to pick from:
· Light (in the full page, left): paper #F7F3EE, fragments orbit and settle into one opportunity card. Calmer, editorial, reads instantly.
· Night archive (right): deep aubergine, a receding ranked index tilted into depth like a card catalog at night. More atmospheric, but the dark opening costs some of the calm-journal register.
Recommendation: light hero as default, Night archive as the dark theme's identity.
Mobile replaces the pinned 3D sequence with a simple stacked progression: scattered source scraps → arrow → the indexed card. No scroll-jacking, 44px+ targets, bottom-sheet nav in production.
